html:
The church of bright onion domes on Red Square in Moscow, built from 1555 to 1561 on the orders of Ivan the Terrible. It marked his capture of Kazan from the Khanate of Kazan in 1552, the first big Russian conquest of a Tatar state.

Its official name is the Cathedral of the Intercession. It is not one hall but nine chapels around a central one, each with its own dome, joined by passages. The popular name comes from Basil the Blessed, a holy fool whose grave was added as a tenth chapel. The bright colours we see now were mostly painted later, in the 1600s.

There is a story that Ivan had the architects blinded so they could never build anything as fine. Historians treat it as legend.

The church stands outside the walls of the Kremlin and has become a symbol of Moscow and of the Russian state itself. Since the 1920s it has been a museum.
